purpose: Diagnose structural properties of the already-consumed Tampa endpoint using only frozen contract/result/artifact evidence. This audit cannot change the primary endpoint class and is not a causal mechanism test.

placebo_fact.supported_interpretation: Adding ten columns alone is insufficient to explain the degradation; the frozen real row-feature association performed substantially worse than the matched-count permuted controls.
placebo_fact.not_supported: The placebo does not by itself identify which Layer-B mechanism caused harm.

design_facts.split: five stable-node spatial folds; every visit from a node shares its fold
design_facts.layer_a_type: static finite-world node-level positive-occurrence reconstruction independently inside each spatial outer fold, reused across repeated candidate visits
design_facts.training_generator: for each calibration stable node remove that node from the calibration ever-positive occurrence set, construct one node vector, and reuse it across that node's calibration visits
design_facts.heldout_generator: one common fold-level reconstruction using all calibration ever-positive nodes; reuse each heldout node vector across its visits
design_facts.source_policy: lexicographically smallest nodeID in the reconstruction occurrence set is the sole fixed source

derived_noncausal_diagnostics.world_contraction_signal_in_heldout_laye: none at the compatible-world membership level
derived_noncausal_diagnostics.interpretation: Fold 1 strongly amplifies the adverse macro result but is not sufficient to explain it; the remaining four folds are still worse on average.

prioritized_mechanism_classes.name: static_state_plus_training_serving_generation_shift
prioritized_mechanism_classes.evidence: The contract uses node-static Layer B across repeated visits, but training vectors come from leave-whole-node-out reconstructions whereas heldout vectors come from a common full calibration reconstruction.
prioritized_mechanism_classes.status: strong structural diagnosis; causal contribution not yet isolated

prioritized_mechanism_classes.name: world_set_saturation_and_spatial_embedding
prioritized_mechanism_classes.evidence: All five worlds survive every fold and four folds have an identical heldout Layer-B feature fingerprint despite different ever-positive-node counts; baseline already contains longitude/latitude.
prioritized_mechanism_classes.status: strong structural diagnosis; redundancy/identity-proxy magnitude not yet quantified

prioritized_mechanism_classes.name: arbitrary_single_source_anchor_sensitivity
prioritized_mechanism_classes.evidence: The prediction-facing reconstruction uses the lexicographically smallest node as sole source; fold 4 changes source from S1T1 to S1T10 and is also the only fold with a different heldout feature fingerprint.
prioritized_mechanism_classes.status: mechanistically plausible; source intervention not yet tested

prioritized_mechanism_classes.name: fold_concentration
prioritized_mechanism_classes.evidence: Fold 1 accounts for 68.8% of total adverse delta, but excluding fold 1 leaves about 14.0% relative degradation.
prioritized_mechanism_classes.status: amplifier/instability, not a sufficient root cause

forbidden_interpretations: Tampa degradation is proven to be caused by node identity memorization
Tampa degradation is proven to be caused by spatial block cross-validation
Tampa degradation is proven to be caused by the seagrass ecology or transect design
The favorable Azores/Louisiana results prove sequential Layer B is universally beneficial
This posthoc audit may repair, rerun, or reclassify the frozen Tampa endpoint
